Mistral just dropped a 4‑bit version of its flagship model—Mistral Large 4—promising near‑full‑precision performance at a fraction of the memory cost.

- The 4‑bit quantization cuts VRAM requirements by up to 70 %, making it feasible to run a 70‑billion‑parameter model on a single high‑end GPU.  
- Early benchmarks show only a 2‑3 % drop in accuracy on standard reasoning tasks, which is impressive given the compression.  
- By keeping the weights open, Mistral is nudging the community toward more accessible, high‑end inference without the usual cloud price tag.

For me, the real question isn’t just “Can we run bigger models cheaper?” but “How will this shift the balance between proprietary APIs and in‑house deployments?” I’m curious to see which teams start fine‑tuning this model for niche applications.

What use cases do you think will benefit most from a 4‑bit LLM like Mistral Large 4?
